title: Homemade Chinese Noodles with Stir-Fried Vegetables
description: Homemade Chinese Noodles with Stir-Fried Vegetables combines fresh hand-cut noodles with crisp colorful vegetables tossed in a savory soy and oyster sauce glaze. The noodles are kneaded, rested, rolled, and cut by hand before being quickly stir-fried over high heat for a glossy restaurant-style finish with authentic wok hei.

ingredients.title: For the Homemade Noodles
items: All-purpose flour – 300 g (2½ cups), high-protein flour preferred

ingredients.title: For the Stir-Fried Vegetables
items: Red bell pepper – ½, thinly sliced
Yellow bell pepper – ½, thinly sliced
Spring onions – 3, cut into 5 cm strips

ingredients.title: For Garnish
items: Chili oil – a few drops, optional

instruction.title: Step 1 – Making the Noodle Dough
steps: Combine the flour and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Gradually add the room-temperature water and vegetable oil while mixing.
Knead until a dough forms.
Continue kneading for approximately 10 minutes until the dough becomes smooth and elastic.
Cover with a damp cloth and rest the dough for 30 minutes.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Rolling & Cutting the Noodles
steps: Transfer the rested dough to a lightly floured work surface.
Roll it into a thin sheet approximately 1–2 mm thick.
Dust the surface generously with flour to prevent sticking.
Fold the dough loosely and cut into thin strips approximately 3–4 mm wide.
Separate the noodles gently and dust lightly with flour if necessary.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Cooking the Noodles
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add the fresh noodles and cook for approximately 2–3 minutes until al dente.
Drain immediately and rinse briefly under cold water to stop the cooking process.
Toss lightly with a small amount of sesame oil to prevent sticking.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Preparing the Sauce
steps: Combine light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, sesame oil, and vegetable stock in a small bowl.
Whisk until the sugar is dissolved and the sauce is evenly combined.
Set aside until ready to stir-fry.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Stir-Frying the Vegetables
steps: Heat a wok over high heat until very hot and lightly smoking.
Add the vegetable or peanut oil.
Add garlic and ginger and stir-fry for approximately 10 seconds until fragrant.
Add carrots, red and yellow bell peppers, and shiitake mushrooms.
Stir-fry for 1–2 minutes while keeping the vegetables crisp.
Add snow peas and spring onions and toss quickly to combine.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Combining Noodles & Sauce
steps: Add the cooked noodles to the hot wok.
Pour the prepared sauce evenly over the noodles and vegetables.
Toss and stir-fry for 1–2 minutes until the noodles are evenly coated and glossy.
Keep the wok moving to develop a smoky wok hei character without overcooking the vegetables.

instruction.title: Step 7 – Presentation & Serving
steps: Use tongs to twirl the noodles into a neat mound on a warm serving plate.
Arrange the colorful vegetables naturally around and over the noodles.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and fresh coriander leaves.
Finish with a few drops of chili oil for color and optional heat.
Serve immediately while hot.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot as a vegetarian Chinese main course.
Pair with vegetable spring rolls, dumplings, or hot and sour soup.
Add tofu, chicken, beef, or shrimp for a protein-rich variation.
Serve immediately after stir-frying to preserve the glossy noodles and crisp vegetables.

chefTips: Use high-protein flour when possible for noodles with a pleasantly chewy, elastic texture.
Resting the dough is essential because it relaxes the gluten and makes rolling and cutting easier.
Cook fresh noodles only until al dente; overcooking makes them soft and difficult to stir-fry.
Keep the wok extremely hot and work quickly to achieve authentic smoky wok hei.
Do not overcrowd the wok, as excess moisture can cause the vegetables and noodles to steam instead of searing.
Maintain a balance between crisp vegetables and chewy noodles by avoiding prolonged stir-frying.
For additional depth, add a small splash of Shaoxing wine immediately after stir-frying the vegetables.
Serve on a warm plate and garnish immediately for the best restaurant-style presentation.
